content.content: #!/usr/bin/env python3 """Port the design package's inner pages into app/nxm/. Runs the package's OWN builders (source/build_page.py, source/build_games2.py) unchanged, intercepting only their last step: instead of base64-inlining images and writing dist/*.html, images are saved to public/nxm/a/ and the assembled page is captured. So the markup/CSS/JS is exactly what was approved; the owner's identity changes are then applied (nxmlib.py). python3 tools/nxm/port_pages.py # every page python3 tools/nxm/port_pages.py vps pricing Outputs per page (generated — edit this script, never the outputs): app/nxm/_pages//page.css every selector scoped to .nxm-p- app/nxm/_pages//content.ts title/description + page markup app/nxm/_pages//script.ts the page's script (nav, reveal, page JS) app/nxm//page.tsx the route Shared: public/nxm/a/. (images, de-duplicated across pages) """ import base64, builtins, hashlib, io, json, os, re, runpy, sys sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))) from nxmlib import (PKG, ROOT, ROUTES, BASE, relink, scope_css, geist, FONT_VARS, swap_buttons, reviews_slot, nav_slots) SRC = f"{PKG}/source" ASSET_DIR = f"{ROOT}/public/nxm/a" os.makedirs(ASSET_DIR, exist_ok=True) # Owner's pick: the live game pages' particle field, on game pages only. # Colours: GAME_VISUAL (components/marketing/GameLogo.tsx) for single-game # pages; the brand pair the live hub/free-tier pages use otherwise. PARTICLES = { "game-servers": ("#3b6be8", "#7b3fef"), "minecraft-server-hosting": ("#3b6d1f", "#6aab3a"), "minecraft-server-hosting-singapore": ("#3b6d1f", "#6aab3a"), "free-minecraft": ("#8a70fb", "#22d3ee"), } # Page content fixes the package flagged against the live site (OPEN-ITEMS §C) # or the owner decided (IDENTITY-SPEC). (old, new) pairs, asserted to apply. FIXES = { "matrix": [("Claude CLI", "Claude Code")], # a stray in the design's markup: harmless in the standalone file # (the browser ignores it), but inside the page wrapper it closes the # wrapper early and breaks hydration "vps-vs-digitalocean": [("\n", "\n")], } from html.parser import HTMLParser _VOID = {"area","base","br","col","embed","hr","img","input","link","meta","source","track","wbr"} def balanced(html): """Stray end tags (no matching open element) — each one would close the page wrapper when the markup is injected, so a page with any fails.""" class P(HTMLParser): def __init__(self): super().__init__(convert_charrefs=True); self.st = []; self.stray = [] def handle_starttag(self, t, a): if t not in _VOID: self.st.append(t) def handle_startendtag(self, t, a): pass def handle_endtag(self, t): if t in _VOID: return if t in self.st: while self.st and self.st.pop() != t: pass else: self.stray.append((t, self.getpos())) p = P(); p.feed(html); p.close() return p.stray # ── real-data wiring: tools/nxm/wire/.py ────────────────────────────── # A wire module replaces the design's snapshot data with slots/data the page's # loader (app/nxm/_data/.ts) fills from the system at request time: # body(html) -> html snapshot markup -> {{nxm:key}} slots # js(src) -> src snapshot constants -> window.__NXM values # ALLOW = {...} $-amounts that are NOT ours (competitor prices, etc.) import importlib.util sys.path.insert(0, f"{os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))}/wire") def load_wire(slug): f = f"{os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))}/wire/{slug.replace('-', '_')}.py" if not os.path.exists(f): return None spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(f"wire_{slug}", f) m = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec); spec.loader.exec_module(m) return m PRICE = re.compile(r"\$\s?\d[\d,]*(?:\.\d\d)?") NUMPRICE = re.compile(r"""["']?\b(?:p|i|r|pr|price|priceUsd|from)["']?\s*:\s*\d+\.\d\d\b""") def audit(slug, body, js, allow): """Every $-amount left in a page must be allowed (not ours). Returns the stale ones; a page with any is not launch-ready.""" text = re.sub(r"<[^>]+>", " ", body) + " " + js found = {m.group(0) for m in PRICE.finditer(text)} # prices held as bare numbers in data constants / JSON (p: 12.78, "price":4.99) found |= {m.group(0) for m in NUMPRICE.finditer(text)} return sorted(found - set(allow)) def js_buttons(js): """Buttons built by the design's scripts get the same hierarchy.""" js = re.sub(r"class=\"btn \$\{([^}]*?)\s*\?\s*'btn-grad'\s*:\s*'btn-ghost'\}\"", lambda m: f'class="${{{m.group(1)} ? \'nxm-btn\' : \'nxm-glassbtn\'}}"', js) js = re.sub(r"class=\"au-btn \$\{([^}]*?)\s*\?\s*''\s*:\s*'au-btn--ghost'\}\"", lambda m: f'class="${{{m.group(1)} ? \'nxm-btn\' : \'nxm-ghost\'}}"', js) js, _ = swap_buttons(js) return js # ── run a package builder, capturing its output ──────────────────────────── _blobs = {} STATUS = {} def _fake_b64(data, *a, **k): h = hashlib.sha1(data).hexdigest()[:16] _blobs[h] = data return ("NXMA" + h).encode() def build(slug): cap = {} real_open, real_b64 = builtins.open, base64.b64encode class Cap(io.StringIO): def __init__(self, key): super().__init__(); self.key = key def close(self): cap[self.key] = self.getvalue(); super().close() def __exit__(self, *a): self.close() def fake_open(path, mode="r", *a, **k): p = str(path) if "w" in mode and ("/dist/" in p or os.path.basename(p).startswith("test")): return Cap(os.path.basename(p)) return real_open(path, mode, *a, **k) cwd = os.getcwd(); os.chdir(SRC) builtins.open, base64.b64encode = fake_open, _fake_b64 try: if slug == "game-servers": sys.argv = ["build_games2.py"]; runpy.run_path("build_games2.py", run_name="__main__") else: sys.argv = ["build_page.py", slug]; runpy.run_path("build_page.py", run_name="__main__") finally: builtins.open, base64.b64encode = real_open, real_b64 os.chdir(cwd) html = next(v for k, v in cap.items() if k.startswith("nxeon-")) return html # ── native pages: pages the design package doesn't include ───────────────── # Authored in the package's own page format (body.html with {{SPRITE}}/{{NAV}}/ # {{FOOTER}}, page.css, page.js, meta.json) under tools/nxm/native// and # assembled exactly like the package's build_page.py: shared shell + common.css # + aurora + the page's own css/js. Then the same pipeline as every page. NATIVE = f"{os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))}/native" def build_native(slug): D = f"{NATIVE}/{slug}/" meta = json.load(open(D + "meta.json")) p1, p2, p3 = (open(f"{SRC}/part{i}.html").read() for i in (1, 2, 3)) MAIN = "https://claude.ai/artifact/KryegJ1sG3zYzX7MyxypYs" head = re.sub(r".*?", f"{meta['title']}", p1, count=1) head = re.sub(r'', f'', head, count=1) head = head.replace('url("__IMG_HERO2__")', "none").replace('url("__IMG_GRAIN__")', "none") css = open(f"{SRC}/pages/common.css").read() + AURORA_CSS + (open(D + "page.css").read() if os.path.exists(D + "page.css") else "") head = head.replace("", css + "", 1) sprite = p2[p2.index("") + 6:p2.index("") + 6] local = set(meta.get("anchors", [])) def fix_links(h): h = re.sub(r'href="#([a-z-]*)"', lambda m: f'href="#{m.group(1)}"' if (m.group(1) in local or m.group(1).startswith("i-")) else f'href="{MAIN}#{m.group(1)}"', h) return h.replace(f'href="{MAIN}#top"', f'href="{MAIN}"') nav = fix_links(p2[p2.index('") + 9]).replace(f'href="{MAIN}#main"', 'href="#main"') nav = nav.replace('") + 9]) body = open(D + "body.html").read() for k, v in {"SPRITE": sprite, "NAV": nav, "FOOTER": footer, "MAIN": MAIN}.items(): body = body.replace("{{" + k + "}}", v) helpers = p3[p3.index("\n\n\n" html = head + body + js A = f"{PKG}/assets/" m = {k: (v if v.startswith("/") else A + v) for k, v in meta.get("assets", {}).items()} m.setdefault("LOGO", A + "logo.png") for _k in ["minecraft", "rust", "palworld", "valheim", "ark", "cs2"]: m.setdefault("NAV_" + _k.upper(), A + "nav/" + _k + ".webp") mime = lambda q: "image/png" if q.endswith(".png") else "image/svg+xml" if q.endswith(".svg") else "image/jpeg" if q.endswith(".jpg") else "image/webp" for k in sorted(m, key=len, reverse=True): html = html.replace(f"__IMG_{k}__", f"data:{mime(m[k])};base64," + _fake_b64(open(m[k], "rb").read()).decode()) left = set(re.findall(r"__IMG_[A-Za-z0-9_]+__", html)); assert not left, left return html EXT = {"image/png": "png", "image/webp": "webp", "image/jpeg": "jpg", "image/svg+xml": "svg", "image/gif": "gif"} def externalise(s): def rep(m): h = m.group(2); ext = EXT.get(m.group(1), "bin") path = f"{ASSET_DIR}/{h}.{ext}" if not os.path.exists(path): open(path, "wb").write(_blobs[h]) return f"/nxm/a/{h}.{ext}" s = re.sub(r"data:([\w/+.-]+);base64,NXMA([0-9a-f]{16})", rep, s) assert "NXMA" not in s return s AURORA_CSS = open(f"{SRC}/pages/aurora.css").read() AURORA_JS = open(f"{SRC}/pages/aurora.built.js").read() def port(slug): html = externalise(build_native(slug) if os.path.isdir(f"{NATIVE}/{slug}") else build(slug)) head, rest = html.split("", 1) title = re.search(r"(.*?)", head).group(1) desc_m = re.search(r'([\s\S]*)", head).group(1) assert AURORA_CSS in css, "aurora.css not found verbatim" css = geist(css.replace(AURORA_CSS, "")) scope, rootcls = f".nxm-p-{slug}", f":root.nxm-p-{slug}-root" # the design's : its classes, CSS variables and data-* move to the # page wrapper (a nested page can't touch ); `xray` is a class the # design's JS toggles on body btag = re.search(r"]*)>", html).group(1) battr = lambda n: (re.search(rf'{n}="([^"]*)"', btag) or [None, ""])[1] bclasses = battr("class").split() body_attrs = {"cls": " ".join(bclasses), "style": battr("style"), "data": {k: v for k, v in re.findall(r'data-([\w-]+)="([^"]*)"', btag)}} hoisted, rules = scope_css(css, scope, rootcls, frozenset(bclasses) | {"xray"}) extra = (f"\n{scope}{{{FONT_VARS}}}\n" f"{rootcls}{{--nav-h:68px;background:#060913}}\n" f"{scope} .nv-sheet-f .nxm-navcta:only-child{{grid-column:1/-1}}\n" f"{scope} .nxm-navcta{{white-space:nowrap}}\n" f"{scope} .nv-sheet-f .nxm-navcta{{height:48px;justify-content:center;font-size:1rem}}\n" f"@media (max-width:1080px){{{scope} .nv-act>.nxm-navcta{{display:none}}}}\n") css_out = ("/* GENERATED by tools/nxm/port_pages.py from the design package — do not edit. */\n" + "\n".join(hoisted) + "\n" + "\n".join(rules) + extra) # Markup: everything between and the page script. js_at = rest.rfind("", js).group(1) assert AURORA_JS in js, "aurora.built.js not found verbatim" js = js.replace(AURORA_JS, "") js = js.replace("https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/three.js/r128/three.min.js", "/nxm/three.min.js") # body attributes now live on the page wrapper js = js.replace("document.body.dataset", "document.querySelector('.nxm-p').dataset") js = The page's own script.\n" f"export const PAGE_SCRIPT = {json.dumps(js)};\n") route = ROUTES[slug] loader = wire is not None and os.path.exists(f"{ROOT}/app/nxm/_data/{slug}.ts") static = bool(wire is not None and getattr(wire, "STATIC", False)) assert wire is None or loader or static, f"{slug}: wire module without app/nxm/_data/{slug}.ts" has_meta = loader and "export async function meta" in open(f"{ROOT}/app/nxm/_data/{slug}.ts").read() for r, fixed in routes_for(slug): if ("[" in r or fixed) and not has_meta: STATUS[slug] = STATUS.get(slug, "") + f" (route {r} not written: template needs its loader)" continue write_route(slug, r, fixed, loader) print(f"{slug:36} {BASE}{route if route != '/' else ''} css {len(css_out)//1024}KB body {len(body)//1024}KB " f"js {len(js)//1024}KB buttons {btns} reviews {nrev}") return slug # ── routes ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── # A page is a TEMPLATE when its route has [params] (e.g. /mods/[family]/[slug]) # or when tools/nxm/routes/.json fans it out to many fixed routes # (e.g. the game template -> /rust-server-hosting {family: "rust"}, ...). # Loaders get the params: load(p) / meta(p). def routes_for(slug): f = f"{os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))}/routes/{slug}.json" if os.path.exists(f): return [(e["route"], e.get("params", {})) for e in json.load(open(f))] return [(ROUTES[slug], {})] def write_route(slug, route, fixed, loader): """One route file. particles = f' particles={{{{ from: "{pc[0]}", to: "{pc[1]}" }}}}' if pc else "" # loader-supplied colours (e.g. per game) win over the slug default pdefault = f' ?? {{ from: "{pc[0]}", to: "{pc[1]}" }}' if pc else "" has_meta = loader and "export async function meta" in open(f"{ROOT}/app/nxm/_data/{slug}.ts").read() dyn = "[" in route assert not (dyn or fixed) or has_meta, f"{slug}: template routes need a loader with meta(p) for SEO" path_expr = ("`" + re.sub(r"\[(\w+)\]", r"${p.\1}", route) + "`") if dyn else json.dumps(route) if loader: imp = (f'import {{ load{", meta" if has_meta else ""} }} from "{rel}/_data/{slug}";\n' f'import type {{ NxmLoad }} from "{rel}/_data/lib";\n' f'import {{ nxmParams }} from "{rel}/_data/params";\n') ptype = "{ params: Promise>; searchParams: Promise> }" getp = f"const p = await nxmParams(params, searchParams, {json.dumps(fixed)});" metacall = f"nxmMetadata({path_expr}, await meta(p))" if has_meta else f"nxmMetadata({path_expr})" body = f"""export 1	/**
2	 * Game family × location landing pages — the SEO matrix crossing every real,
3	 * currently-sellable game family against a country/region-level location
4	 * list ("Singapore Minecraft Server Hosting", "Germany Valheim Server
5	 * Hosting"), plus general "[Location] VPS Hosting" / "[Location] Game Server
6	 * Hosting" pages for the locations that don't already have an equivalent
7	 * page via lib/marketing/locationLandings.ts's existing city/region matrix.
8	 *
9	 * ARCHITECTURE: deliberately modeled on `buildLanding`/`buildRegionLanding`
10	 * in locationLandings.ts (same file this reuses `BuiltLanding`, `listPhrase`
11	 * and the `presence`-driven honesty discipline from) rather than the 40
12	 * hand-written `*-server-hosting/page.tsx` files — one data table here, wired
13	 * into the SAME `app/(marketing)/[slug]/page.tsx` route and the SAME
14	 * `app/sitemap.ts` loop as the rest of the location matrix, so there is still
15	 * exactly one route file and the sitemap can never drift from the real slug
16	 * list. Real pricing is NEVER hardcoded here: every combo's `GamePlanRow[]`
17	 * (or VPS `LandingPlan[]` for the general pages) is fetched live by the route
18	 * from `db.gamePlan` / `db.plan` and passed in — this module only turns
19	 * already-real numbers into prose and a spec note.
20	 *
21	 * HONESTY. Nxeon operates exactly two real datacenters — Singapore (`sgp1`)
22	 * and Falkenstein, Germany (`fsn1`) — see lib/node-regions.ts. Every
23	 * `GameLocationDef` below carries the same `presence` field as
24	 * `LocationDef` in locationLandings.ts ("datacenter" | "network" | "market"),
25	 * set from real geography, not marketing convenience:
26	 *   - "datacenter": Singapore, Germany (the two real DCs), plus Southeast
27	 *     Asia and Europe — the immediate regions those two DCs physically sit
28	 *     inside, so the same honest claim applies at one level up.
29	 *   - "network": Malaysia, Indonesia, United Kingdom, Netherlands — genuinely
30	 *     close to Singapore or Germany (real-world round-trip roughly within
31	 *     the ~40ms "low-ping" bar), so a latency-benefit claim is honestly
32	 *     grounded, but there is no on-site presence — never claim one.
33	 *   - "market": United States, North America, Canada, South Korea, Japan,
34	 *     India, Australia — neither real DC is genuinely close to these
35	 *     (measured round-trip is 70-250ms either way, per the 2026-09-24 SEO
36	 *     audit — South Korea/Japan/India/Australia were previously misclassified

content.thinking:
I notice the existing _loc template hardcodes things like the map, tiers, and stats section, so instead I want to build a native page under tools/nxm/native/<slug> that reuses the shared page.css/page.js but restructures the body into slots, with content fully driven by the loader. I'll plan around a single native template slug, something like `location-landing`.

But then routing gets tricky: adding `/[slug]` to ROUTES would make `_is_ported`'s regex match any single-segment path, causing every nxeon.cloud link to get relinked to /nxm/, which would wrongly rewrite other agents' page links like /dashboard. I need to avoid touching ROUTES in a way that triggers that regex, so I'm considering either generating a routes json with explicit concrete routes, or writing my own dynamic route file directly and bypassing ROUTES so port() picks up a routes json instead.

I realize other agents' pages linking to my other location slugs wouldn't get staged automatically since nxmlib only knows exact ROUTES entries. Adding hundreds of ROUTES lines for every slug would be ugly, but PORTED already aggregates entries from all the routes json files, so maybe that's the right place to register the concrete list instead.

The literal "/[slug]" path in PORTED shouldn't matter since nobody actually links to it. content.content:
# Open items

## A. Needs confirmation before launch
1. **Game-server tier prices.** The Minecraft plans (1 GB $2.99 … 16 GB $32.99) are marked as preview figures in the pricing panel; only Valheim's are marked live.
2. **Game-server CPU and NVMe specs are placeholders**, modelled on the VPS plans: 1 GB = 1 vCPU/15 GB, 2 GB = 1/25, 4 GB = 2/50, 6 GB = 2/65, 8 GB = 3/80, 12 GB = 4/100, 16 GB = 4/120. Edit `SPEC` in `source/build_gs2.py`.
3. **Fit-calculator and modpack-guide numbers are sizing heuristics.** Edit `PACK` in `pages/_gs3.js` and `TINFO` in `build_gs2.py`.
4. **Nav links with unknown routes.** Dedicated IPv4 points to /vps#ipv4, and "AI apps and agents" points to /features.
5. **Custom / enterprise route.** Custom-server CTAs go to `/contact?topic=custom`. Confirm, or supply a dedicated enterprise page or booking link.
6. **Review badges.** Trustpilot 4.9 (312), HostAdvice 4.8 (148) and Google 4.9 (205) are copied from the live site, where they link to `#`. Verify the figures and link them to the real profiles.
7. **Routes marked TBD** in `docs/url-map.json`: NxCloud, game × location pages, and the mods browse page.
8. **Logged-in nav state.** "My account" / "Back to portal" go in the Log in / Get started slot.

## B. Pages still to build (templates exist for most)
- **From existing templates:**
  - the other ~46 game-server pages (`build_gs2.py`: add a game dict like `MC`)
  - game × location pages
  - a Valheim rebuild on the new template
  - regenerating Minecraft in Falkenstein
- **Comparisons:** 9 remaining (Hostinger, GoDaddy, Bluehost, Namecheap, HostGator, Cloudways, IONOS, Kamatera, A2 Hosting). Needs competitor logos and current pricing; add entries to `CMP` in `build_compare.py`.
- **Migration guides:** the 10 "migrate from [host]" pages.
- **NxLabs, other games:** mods pages for the other 32 games (`build_modsgame.py`), and more mod pages (`build_modpage.py`). Add more illustrations to `mod_tags.py` for the categories that matter.
- **Blog:**
  - the full archive and category pages (the hub currently holds 25 real guides)
  - covers for every guide via the visual system
- **New designs:**
  - Vibe coding
  - Features (Claude AI builder)
  - Server directory
  - Free tools hub, plus Minecraft server status, server size calculator and ping/latency test
  - Status
  - About, Security, Developers, Docs and Affiliate
  - Cheap VPS, Gaming VPS, Block storage and Game-server mod support
  - Legal: Terms, Privacy, Acceptable Use and SLA
- **Wiring:** the contact form, newsletter and "Add to my server" flows are demos and need backends.

## C. Issues found on the live site
- **Matrix:** the stats band shows "0 consoles", "~$0" and "0%" because the count-up never runs.
- **Contact:** reads "~1 one business day", a typo.
- **Support promise is inconsistent:** "within one business day" (Contact) vs "24/7 support" and "answers around the clock" elsewhere.
- **Pricing contradicts itself:** "never increases at renewal" vs "intro price for your first term, then … regular price".
- **Managed vs self-managed:** both claims appear.
- **Regions:** the homepage "global network" section lists Toronto, New York, Amsterdam, Frankfurt, Singapore, Tokyo and Sydney, while the site elsewhere says Singapore and Germany data centres only.
- **Blog:**
  - an unrelated game-server panel screenshot appears inside non-game articles (Vaultwarden, Linux tuning)
  - the internal tag `#seobatch` is public (tag list and article meta)
  - index cards mostly lack dates
  - "Read more" appears inconsistently
- **Naming:** the site mixes "Claude CLI" and "Claude Code"; Anthropic's product is Claude Code.
- **Imagery:** the panel screenshots and renders show a real-looking server IP (178.63.94.114). One render lists a Canada location and old prices. The mods collage uses recognisable game characters.

"""THE location template (native: tools/nxm/native/location-landing, the
design's location page extended): every generated location landing the live
site serves from app/(marketing)/[slug] plus the Singapore landers, served
under /nxm by the hand-written dispatcher app/nxm/[slug]/page.tsx (one
dynamic route instead of ~770 route files; game x location combos go through
the game x location template there). The whole page is slots: copy from the
live builders (lib/marketing/*Landings.ts), plans/regions from the DB — see
app/nxm/_data/location-landing.ts.

Port time only draws the dotted world map (public/nxm/loc/world.webp) from
the design's own land mask (assets/geo/mask.b64, 256x128 equirectangular),
for places neither regional map (apac/eu) covers. Keep WORLD in sync with
LOC_MAPS.world in app/nxm/_data/location-geo.ts.
"""
import base64, os
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))))
PKG = "/root/nxeon-marketing-v1/src/New Marketing Website v1/nxeon-website-handoff"
WORLD = dict(W=1600, H=634, lon=(-135, 145), lat=(-45, 66))


def world_map():
    mask = base64.b64decode(open(f"{PKG}/assets/geo/mask.b64").read().strip())
    gw, gh, cell = 256, 128, 360 / 256
    s = 2  # supersample, then downscale for smooth dots
    W, H = WORLD["W"] * s, WORLD["H"] * s
    img = Image.new("RGBA", (W, H), (0, 0, 0, 0))
    d = ImageDraw.Draw(img)
    (lo0, lo1), (la0, la1) = WORLD["lon"], WORLD["lat"]
    r = 2.5 * s
    for y in range(gh):
        lat = 90 - (y + 0.5) * cell
        if not (la0 <= lat <= la1):
            continue
        for x in range(gw):
            i = y * gw + x
            if not (mask[i >> 3] >> (i & 7)) & 1:
                continue
            lon = -180 + (x + 0.5) * cell
            if not (lo0 <= lon <= lo1):
                continue
            px = (lon - lo0) / (lo1 - lo0) * W
            py = (la1 - lat) / (la1 - la0) * H
            # a soft vertical tint: cyan in the south, violet in the north (the brand pair)
            t = (lat - la0) / (la1 - la0)
            col = (int(96 + 60 * t), int(170 - 40 * t), 255, 150)
            d.ellipse((px - r, py - r, px + r, py + r), fill=col)
    img = img.resize((WORLD["W"], WORLD["H"]), Image.LANCZOS)
    out = f"{ROOT}/public/nxm/loc/world.webp"
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(out), exist_ok=True)
    img.save(out, "WEBP", quality=88, method=6)


def body(s):
    world_map()
    return s


def js(s):
    # the page script reads the local-clock zone from the loader's data
    return s

## Location landings + Singapore landers + server directory: done (staging `/nxm` only, nothing committed)

**Outcome:** every generated location landing the live `app/(marketing)/[slug]` serves now renders under `/nxm`, plus the five Singapore landers and the three server-directory routes. A loader run over all 770 slugs finished with **770 ok, 0 failed**: every slot filled, a title and description on each, Product JSON-LD on each, and no "ms" latency figures anywhere. Typecheck of my files is clean. I spot-checked 30+ pages over HTTP on :3033 and all returned 200. Unknown slugs return 404, and so does stationeers, which the live matrix also excludes.

I applied your owner direction. When the enabled regions differ from the two the live copy names, the page now logs a `console.warn` and keeps rendering. The map, distances, stats and deploy links all use the enabled `db.node` rows, so a deploy link can only point at an enabled region. A city in the live tables that has no coordinates also only warns and is left off the map; nothing is dropped or hidden.

### Route counts
| Family | Count | Served by |
|---|---|---|
| `REGION_LANDING_SLUGS` | 18 | `/nxm/[slug]`, location template |
| `LANDING_SLUGS` (city matrix) | 108 | 107 via `/nxm/[slug]`; `germany-vps-hosting` keeps its existing page, unchanged |
| `GENERAL_LOCATION_SLUGS` | 24 | location template |
| `GAME_LOCATION_SLUGS` | 615 | game×location template (the page `/minecraft-server-hosting/singapore` uses) |
| Singapore landers | 5 | location template, same builder and plan source as the live pages |
| Directory | `/servers`, `/game-servers/directory`, `/servers/[subdomain]` | new native pages |

`/nxm/[slug]` is **one hand-written dynamic route** that resolves slugs with the live `find*` and `build*` functions. Static `/nxm` routes still win: vps, singapore-vps-hosting, germany-vps-hosting, `/minecraft-server-hosting/singapore`, pricing, about and others still render their own pages. One `/nxm/vps` request returned a single 404 while :3033 was auto-restarting; ten later requests were 200 with the right page.

### Honesty and SEO
- **Copy:** all titles, H1s, intro, why, steps, FAQ and related links come verbatim from `lib/marketing/locationLandings.ts` and `gameLocationLandings.ts`, including their `presence` framing.
- **Hero text I added on game×location pages:** the H1 says "…servers in X. Hosted in Falkenstein/Singapore." only where there is a real datacenter; everywhere else it reads "…servers for American players." The hero note is the location's `hub` sentence, verbatim.
- **Maps:** they show straight-line km to the nearest enabled datacenter, with the caveat that real ping depends on the route. No latency numbers.
- **Deploy links:** a region is pre-selected only where the live copy treats the place as near a datacenter (or the live game×location code picks a nearest region); otherwise the customer picks at checkout.
- **Structured data:** every page gets canonical, BreadcrumbList and FAQPage (FAQ counts match live). Location pages also get Product/AggregateOffer from real plans, the directories a CollectionPage/ItemList when servers are listed, and server pages a GameServer entry.

### Data sources
- **Plans:** `db.plan` for VPS-type pages, `db.hostingPlan` plus the first-month-free check for web hosting, and `db.gamePlan` / `sellableGames` for game pages.
- **Game×location pages:** the game template's own `gamePage` data (tiers, configurator, mods, sizing), with honest location slots layered on top.
- **Regions:** enabled `db.node` rows and `REGION_COORDS`.
- **Directory:** the same queries and privacy gate as the live pages, and the same bounded 4-second SSH status check on the server page.

### Could not source or verify
- **Directory with real servers:** the staging DB has 0 public free servers and 0 listed paid ones. The directories render their empty state, and `/servers/<anything>` returns 404. I checked the card and server-page design only by injecting SAMPLE rows into the page in the browser; nothing was saved. The live SSH status path was not exercised.
- **Missing flags:** South Korea shows a blank flag chip on game×location pages because the game template's CSS has no `kr` flag. Brussels, Dublin and San Juan get a neutral disc because no flag asset exists for them.

### Decisions for the owner
1. **Game-server price anchor.** The generic "(place) Game Server Hosting" pages price off game plans, as the live Singapore lander does, so the copy says "from $2.99/mo". The live generic pages use VPS plans and say "from $8.99".
2. **City web-hosting pages** use `db.hostingPlan`, as the live Singapore web lander does; the live generic pages show VPS plans.
3. **Duplicate content.** `/singapore-minecraft-server-hosting` (live matrix) and the new `/minecraft-server-hosting/singapore` will both exist.
4. **"Recommended" tag.** I added it to the plan whose RAM matches each page's own sizing note; there is no "popular" flag for VPS plans in the DB.
5. **Directory FAQs.** I added five, all built from existing live wording; please review.
6. **Broken live link.** The live `/game-servers/directory` CTA points to `/free-minecraft-hosting`, which looks like a dead link; mine points to `/free-minecraft`.
7. **Page weight.** The `[slug]` route loads both templates' CSS (about 212 KB and 378 KB) on every location page.
8. **Multi-timezone places** such as the US show the first-listed city's time in the game template's "Local time" chip.

### Shared-file notes
- I added ROUTES lines in `tools/nxm/nxmlib.py`: `location-landing` with a concrete example route so it doesn't match every single-segment path, `server-directory` and `server-detail`.
- I added `/servers` and `/game-servers/directory` to `app/nxm/_seo/registry.ts`.
- The free-minecraft page's link to `/servers` will point inside `/nxm` on its next port.
- `tools/nxm/README.md` and `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` don't yet mention the `[slug]` dispatcher; I left both alone.
